title: Read the whole story first
summary: Build a quick story map before filling any gap, then test each word against grammar, meaning and the passage as a whole.

sections.title: Retell before you fill
content: Read a short story once without stopping. State who is involved, where they are, what problem appears and how the situation ends.
A cloze passage is a connected story. A word that fits one sentence can still be wrong if it breaks the chronology or tone.

sections.title: Use a three-filter routine
content: Whole-story filter: identify the setting, characters, event order, conflict and final mood before choosing words.
Grammar filter: decide whether each gap needs a noun, verb, adjective or adverb, and check tense and agreement.
Meaning filter: read the full sentence with the candidate inserted, then reread the sentences before and after it.
Do not force the first plausible word. More words are supplied than gaps, so several distractors are designed to fit the topic but not the exact context.

sections.title: Map the story before opening the bank
content: Example map: setting—community radio station during a storm; characters—Maya, a presenter and an electrician; conflict—the microphones fail; resolution—the damaged plug is repaired; tone—anxiety changes to relief.
For “the studio was unusually ___”, grammar asks for an adjective. The story map then rules out feelings that describe people and favours a word describing an empty place.
For “the programme would be ___ unless…”, chronology signals a possible future consequence, so the answer must describe a delayed event rather than a past repair.

sections.title: Annotate each gap
content: Beside every gap, note the required word class and one clue from the nearby sentence. Connect any gap whose answer depends on the earlier problem or later resolution.
Choose the most constrained gaps first. Leave uncertain gaps blank until the remaining bank becomes easier to compare.

sections.title: Complete a full passage
content: Read all three paragraphs first. Fill the eight gaps from a twelve-word bank. Each word can be used once, and four words will remain unused.
Before submitting, reread the completed story from beginning to end instead of checking each sentence in isolation.

sections.title: Diagnose the failed filter
content: Missed clue: the surrounding words or story event pointed elsewhere.
Option trap: the word matched the topic but not the sentence.
Tone mismatch: the word had the wrong feeling or strength.
Unknown meaning: the word or a close alternative was unfamiliar. Record the closest cause before retrying the passage.

sections.title: The afternoon broadcast
content: Complete one original narrative passage. Feedback appears only after every gap has an answer so that no early result reveals a later choice.
